brands.d: Family-owned Dearborn, Michigan workwear house founded by Hamilton Carhartt, known for duck jackets, overalls and coveralls.
Carhartt Work In Progress, the European streetwear line that recuts Carhartt classics such as the Michigan Coat and Detroit Jacket.
Fort Worth, Texas workwear brand of Williamson-Dickie, begun as a denim bib-overall maker and famous for the 874 work pant.
San Francisco workwear brand founded by the grandson of riveted-jeans inventor Jacob Davis, known for heavyweight poly-cotton twill.
Texas workwear maker founded by Earl Beard in Crockett, known for painter pants and fatigue pants.
Nashville, Tennessee workwear company supplying industrial and uniform-rental trousers and shirts.
Salina, Kansas denim brand of H.D. Lee, now owned by Kontoor Brands, which built its name on the 1911 bib overall.
Oshkosh, Wisconsin children's apparel company, a Carter's subsidiary, best known for children's bib overalls.
Overalls, jeans and chore coats made by the King family's L.C. King Manufacturing in Bristol, Tennessee.
Shawnee, Oklahoma maker of bib overalls and jeans cut from American-grown cotton denim.
Brighton-based brand of Lucy Greenwood and Christopher Renwick known for colourful, gender-neutral dungarees.
Normandy house whose moleskin work jacket, made since 1913 for Breton and Norman farm workers, is the reference bleu de travail.
Family-run French workwear maker producing hydrone-blue work jackets in its own factory in western France since 1927.
French maker of moleskin and drill bleu de travail work jackets and trousers.
Nottingham menswear label founded by David Keyte, whose Bakers Jacket is a modern chore-coat staple.
German maker of dated reproductions of mid-century US military and workwear patterns.
Los Angeles denim and workwear maker known for the Supply Jacket in waxed canvas and selvedge denim.
French motorcycle-wear brand with work-inspired jackets and trousers such as the Craftsman Jacket.

traditions.d: French labourers' blue work clothing — moleskin or drill jackets and trousers — now reproduced by heritage makers.

traditions.mat: Cotton moleskin, drill, twill, denim in hydrone blue
traditions.auth: Thick cotton moleskin or drill, hydrone-blue dye that fades with wear, made-in-France labels and simple unlined construction.
